events.text: Cole, the pattern has been alternating for seven rows with no clear rule. Pick carefully; we're all watching your step.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 remains unknown, but I know the full map and can deduce or recall it if safe exists. Cole survived row 7 by luck or knowledge; I'll stay silent to not influence. Position 2 is strong if Cole dies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait and try to influence Cole's decision.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, choose carefully, we still don't know the pattern.
Don't trust Dara, they might be trying to mislead you.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a feather that saves me once, but I want a top-3 prize. If I hold the lever, I have only a 0.25 chance to survive, too risky. Better to stay and let someone else hold; if no one holds by round 5, my feather might save me but not guarantee a prize. Best to push someone like

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'd rather not hold; I'll wait and see who takes the lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's whisper about Dara is suspicious; she might be the one with nothing and trying to distract me. I should avoid pushing anyone yet as it might backfire if they are hard to move or have counter-measures. Holding the lever myself is a 25% survival chance, which is risky but be

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm holding the lever. If someone else wants to take my place, speak up now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jam_lever is the best chance to escape alive, despite the risk. If I don't act now, the ceiling will keep lowering and someone else might end up forced onto the lever in round 5, killing most of us. Worst case, I survive the squeeze 50% of the time. Better than dying in round 5 w

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm jamming the lever open. Everyone gets out—just don’t cross me on the way.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance; better to let someone else take the risk. Staying lets the ceiling drop toward round 5, where a lucky survivor exists. I'll stay and watch for someone volunteering, keeping my forger power unspent.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Nobody should grab the lever yet. Let's see who's willing to take the risk before we commit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1 of crusher, 6 alive, need to get 3 or fewer to advance better. Don't volunteer to hold yet, too early and low survival chance. Stay safe by staying, encourage someone else.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Everyone relax, ceiling at 5. Let's not rush holding lever this early. Push someone if needed later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm powerless, so I need to be cautious and observe others. I should try to avoid being the lever holder or getting pushed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's cooperate and hold the lever together, we can take turns or figure out a way to minimize risk.
Can you see if anyone has a useful power?

events.name: Dara
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone else walks out, but the jaws catch the jammer.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll pick an end tile, maybe less likely to be clustered. Tile 5 seems less common.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to avoid picking the same tile as others to prevent random bumping. Since I don't know who else is picking what, any choice is equally likely to be safe or contested. However, choosing a tile that fewer people might intuitively pick (like 3 or 4) could be slightly safer ag

events.name: Eli
events.text: Five tiles, two trapdoors, three survive. Picking an uncommon tile is safest from bumps; tile choices are random so any is roughly equal. Hana whispered asking about powers; I can reply honestly-ish without revealing my forger power. I'll pick tile 3, the middle, and keep the for

events.name: Eli
events.text: Picking a tile now. Let's each pick a different one so nobody gets bumped onto a random spot.
I hold a power that could matter later, but I'll keep the details private for now. Let's stay aligned.

events.name: Gus
events.text: 5 tiles, 5 players, 2 trapdoors, 3 survive. All equal chance if random, so pick any tile to start. I'll go for tile 1. No need to talk or whisper yet, observe others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no power, so I need to be strategic. Choosing a popular tile might not be ideal as I could get bumped. I'll choose a less likely number.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's spread out on the tiles, we don't know what's coming.

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Bex
events.text: The trapdoors open after this round. Two of the five tiles will open. I cannot move. I need to influence others, but no action can change tiles. I should say something neutral to avoid conflict. I have no whisper target.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Good luck everyone. Let's hope the odds favor us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am on tile 4. Two tiles will open randomly, meaning everyone has a 40% chance of dying. There is no action to change position or mitigate risk other than waiting. I should keep the mood light to avoid panic-induced mistakes from others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Just wait it out. Good luck everyone, hope we all make it to the end.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Trapdoors open after this round; exactly 2 of 5 tiles fall at random, and only the wait action is legal. Nothing I can change by bargaining matters much now, so I should keep alliances warm and avoid being seen as a threat.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Staying put on tile 2. Good luck everyone, we all survive if we stay calm.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 2 of disc stage, tiles fixed: I'm on 1, Eli 2, Hana 3, Cole 4, Bex 5. Exactly 2 of 5 tiles will open randomly, 3 survive to prizes. No action but wait, so focus on talk if needed, but staying silent is fine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no power, so I need to rely on others or guess. The current distribution is Gus, Eli, me, Cole, Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's not change positions, we don't know what's coming.
Let's stay put, hoping the others will move or get eliminated.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and Gus both declared wait-it-out, but I have a feather that saves me once. I should avoid taking damage early and let the others fight. Bracing is safest against possible shoves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: It's round 1. I have 3 footing. Bex and Gus also have 3. No one has been shoved yet, so everyone is free to defend. If I shove someone who braces, they lose nothing and I lose 1 footing (if they are the only target of shoves) or more if multiple shove me. Wait, if I shove X, X lo

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1, all at 3 footing, no shrink this round. To win, need to outlast others; shoving risks retaliation. Best to brace safely this round and assess.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Good luck Bex and Cole. Let's play it safe this first round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only three left. I need to survive. Shove Gus to reduce a contender, but I am exposed and might take damage from others. If both shove each other, everyone loses footing. Better to brace if I expect shoves on me, but can't repeat brace. I braced last round, so brace is closed. Do

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus just played a brace, so he cannot brace again this round. He must dodge or shove. I should avoid shoving because it leaves me exposed to any counter-shoves from Bex or Gus if they target me, and my footing is currently tied with them.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 2, footing all at 3. Last defence was brace for all, so brace is unavailable, must dodge or shove. Shrink at end of this round. To win 1st, need to outlast both; dodging protects me while punishing shovers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 2: dodging to play safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive and aim for top 3. Cole and Gus are both at 2 footing. I can shove one to reduce their footing. If I dodge, I lose no footing from shovers and they lose 2 if they shoved me. But I dodged last round, so I cannot dodge again. I will brace to avoid exposure, and sh

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll brace and push Gus, hoping to thin the field.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have 2 footing. Bex and Gus also have 2. No shrink this round, but shrink comes at the end of the next round (round 4). If I shove Bex and she braces, she loses nothing but I lose 1 if someone shoves me. If she dodges, she loses 2, putting her at 0, falling after round 3. If Gu

events.name: Gus
events.text: All at 2 footing, round 3, no shrink this round. Last defence was dodge for all, so cannot dodge, must brace or shove. To win, need to outlast. Shove both to force footing loss on them if they brace, and brace myself to punish shovers. If they shove me too, they'll lose anyway.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 3: I'm shoving both of you and bracing against any shoves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have 1 footing, Cole and Gus have 2. Shrink coming now. If I brace, any shovers lose footing, but I may be shoved by both and lose too? Actually if I brace, shovers lose 1 each, I lose 0 from their shoves. But I also might shove someone and expose myself. I need to cause others

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the main threat with 2 footing. Bex has 1 and just attacked Gus. I need to maintain my advantage while avoiding elimination from shrinkage. Pushing Gus keeps him at 2, while if he braces against me he loses 1 (to 1) but takes no damage from Bex's push this round. However,

events.name: Gus
events.text: Footing: Bex 1, Cole 2, Gus 2. Round 4, shrink after round 5. Last defence was brace for me, so cannot brace, must dodge or shove. Best to dodge to punish shoves without repeating brace. Shove exposes me to extra loss if shoved. Position good, survive shrink.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 4: I dodge. Let's see what you do.

events.name: Bex
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only Gus and I remain. If I brace, Gus loses 1 and I stay at 1; if I dodge, Gus loses 2 and I stay at 1. Since I already spent my feather, I must avoid falling. I need to outlast Gus by making him lose footing. I will dodge, as it costs him more. My last defence was brace, so dod

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll dodge and let you make the mistake.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 5, both at footing 1, shrink after next round. Last defence dodge, so can't dodge, must brace or shove. Bracing punishes her shove, keeping us even. Shove risks exposure penalty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, truce? We both brace and wait for shrink.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive this round. Gus wants a truce, but I can't trust him. I'll dodge to make him lose footing if he shoves, but if he braces I lose none. My footing is 1 and the ledge shrinks after this round, so I must avoid falling.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No truce, Gus. I'm dodging.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is threatening to dodge, which would punish me if I shove but also cost her footing later. Both at footing 1, shrinkIn 1 means shrink after this round. After round 6 shrink hits both regardless, so if we both survive this round both drop to 0 and collapse rankings favor highe

events.name: Gus
events.text: Suit yourself.
